checks.observed: No level-scaling or difficulty-scaling term anywhere in this piece's path. The opening is a dialogue graph over game/data, a keydown handler and a census surface; nothing in it reads a player level.
The one thing that varies with the world is the body: sim.identity.race is a world field, and perturbing it changes four drawn sentences and four writs. Measured — see `consumption`.
No combat, no roll-to-hit and no reward in this piece.
No currency, purchase or economy in the opening. The one thing granted is the stamped writ and the nine root topics _censusFinish() hands over, neither of which is bought.
Nothing in the scene is gated on gold, souls or any resource. The scene is gated on the player walking to a person and pressing a key.
Judged the OUTPUT — drawn rows through getRenderedText, positions through sim.player.pos, five frames — and read source only afterwards, with each read's purpose declared in source_reads.

All three of the round-2 blocking defects are closed and I measured each in play mode with no flags and no harness verbs: census-newgame exit 0 (10 nodes on the player's path, the no-body control still red); a 37-character pangram containing every letter of the alphabet recorded verbatim; opening-play 10 pass / 0 fail reproduced on a quiet box; and the whole scene played to the stamped writ, twice.

§P GATE 1 IS MET. ./play.sh serves a play-mode title with no query string, and from it a person makes a character and walks into the world in about three minutes on a shared four-core box at 3-5 sim fps.

RI-JRN01 is capped by HF5: 1 of M13's 4 released reachability legs has been run over the journey. This is the same charge round 2 made at 2 of 4 and it is not a regression — the keyboard leg went from the title's first two button presses to the whole journey.

The biggest gap is not any of the above: Engine.bodyRace() silently returns null for a body whose race is not in races.json, and the desk then refuses eleven nodes later with round 2's exact sentence behind an authored line. Measured, not theorised.

biggest_gap.what: Engine.bodyRace() ends `return rows.some((r) => r.id === id) ? id : null`. A body whose sim.identity.race is not an id in game/data/progression/races.json is observed as null, SILENTLY, at censusBegin — and Census.answer() throws round 2's exact sentence eleven nodes later, at writ.race-observed. On the player's path that throw is caught and rendered as the single authored refusal line, so the player reads 'She stops writing, and does not look up. — No. Not in that box, and not in those words.' in front of a door that is held shut, with no way forward. MEASURED: with sim.identity.race = 'altmer', bodyRace() returns null, titleActivate('new') succeeds, and the scene stops at writ.race-observed.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: This is round 2's soft-lock with a better sentence over it. It is not hypothetical for three reasons. (1) 'altmer' is a real Elder Scrolls race and the Warden-Scribe's OWN written line says it out loud — 'Altmer. — No, of course not, you are not tall enough and you are not smug enough' — it is in writ-house.json's misread table as a wrong guess and not in races.json as a body. (2) At e00e6fe this field's literal WAS an id that is not in races.json: `sim/state.js` line 501 read `race: 'argonian'`. Round 3 changed it to 'saxhleel' and added creation.json starting_body; both are correct, and the class of defect is one bad string away. (3) FOUR things write this field and none validates it — _applyStartingBody(), applyNamedState('race=...'), save/state.js on load, and whatever W1-07 eventually puts in front of the title, which the engine's own comment invites to write it with 'nothing here needs editing'.

remedy.action: Move the guard from Census.answer() at writ.race-observed to Engine.censusBegin(), where the observation is made: if bodyRace() returns null, throw naming the id that was rejected and the file it is missing from. Add tools/check-body-race.mjs (rule 14: a check, not a constructor) reconciling creation.json starting_body, every race literal in game/src/sim/state.js and game/src/save/state.js, and every named state, against game/data/progression/races.json.
remedy.acceptance: (1) A body carrying a race not in races.json is refused at scene START, with the offending id in the message, and the check is watched going RED by planting a bad id. (2) With the assertion armed, all ten races in races.json still complete the scene end to end. (3) census-newgame.mjs still exits 0 and its no-body control still stops.

biggest_gap.acceptance: A body carrying a race not in races.json is refused at scene START with the id named, and the check is watched going red by planting a bad id. And with the assertion armed, all ten races in races.json still complete the scene.
biggest_gap.not_a_hard_fail_because: On the SHIPPED tree the starting body is `saxhleel`, which is a legal id, so no player meets this today — I played through it twice. It is a major defect in the guard, not a live blocker, and the round-2 hard fail it descends from (creation cannot be completed) is genuinely closed.

secondary_observations.what: P9's imperative test is start-anchored and tests grammar, not signposting.
secondary_observations.detail: IMPERATIVE = /^(press|hold|...|go|...)\b/i. 'Go up. The light is bad but it is light.' is CAUGHT. All six of these pass: 'The way out is up the companionway, past the crates.' / 'You will want to go up the stairs behind me.' / 'The desk is up the ladder. They are waiting for you.' / 'Up the ladder, then. That is where they write you down.' / 'I would go up, if I were you.' / the shipped hold.out line. So does the writ.stamp teaching clause the round-2 verdict named as the opening's one tutorial.
secondary_observations.remedy: Keep the imperative test as the register guard it is, and add a second, separate check for WAYFINDING — a drawn string that names a direction, a destination or a next action, however politely — with its own threshold and its own red-team plant. Do not let a green P9 be read as evidence about the doctrine's central claim.

secondary_observations.what: m4_clause1 = 1.03 s is filed as a passing measurement of the build, beside its own 60 s bar.
secondary_observations.detail: journey-run.mjs emits it through led.ok(), not led.unmeasurable(), in the same object as threshold_s: 60. driver_paced: true is a field written and never read back (rule 7's shape) — nothing aggregates on it, so the first tool that counts m4_clause1 rows will count this one as a pass at 1.03 s against a 60 s requirement.
secondary_observations.remedy: Invert it into a build property: hold the driver STILL for 60+ s of simulated time from first_control and assert that NO character-field-writing event appears — no creation_field, no field-writing dialogue_open. That is decidable, it can fail (a build with a timeout on hold.come-to would fire it), it needs no wall clock, and the piece's own 61.5 s wander probe is nine tenths of the way to it. Until then the row should be unmeasurable with why: 'driver-paced'.

corpus_extended.what: RI-JRN01 M9's clause 'no drawn string tells the player what to do' has, in practice, been implemented as a start-anchored imperative regex, and the corpus does not distinguish IMPERATIVE MOOD from WAYFINDING CONTENT.
corpus_extended.why: Six lines that mean 'go up the ladder' pass the shipped test, and so does the writ.stamp clause a previous verdict named as the opening's only tutorial. A build can satisfy M9 completely and still signpost, and this round's hold.out rewrite is exactly the move that exposes it. The item needs either a second measurable clause or an explicit statement that M9 governs register only.

method_deviations.what: critic-w1-26-r3-input.mjs's absolute per-key arrival checks are reported as this critic's own instrument failing, not as the build's.
method_deviations.why: Under stepFrames, pipeline.pressed is an edge cleared by the next latch and page.keyboard.press() is a down-and-up with no frame between them, so Enter and the arrows read dead on a healthy build. Diagnosed, and the assertion moved to rAF where it passes (asaperson A7). The DIFFERENTIAL (shipped vs textFocus nulled) and the TEARDOWN are unaffected by this and both hold.

method_deviations.what: opening-play.mjs was run to a scratch shots directory rather than its default.
method_deviations.why: Its default writes docs/shots/2026-08-08-w1-26-r2-*.png, which are the round-2 critic's named evidence. Recorded as OBS-9 rather than worked around silently.

method_deviations.what: leak, input and consume set play-instrumented and use stepFrames for SETUP.
method_deviations.why: What is under test in those three is content, the keydown handler and the model, not the frame source. The one probe whose claim is about the frame source — asaperson — uses rAF, no flags, and no harness mutator at all. Declared in each tool's header.

arbitration_questions.question: Does RI-JRN01 M13's HF5 fire on legs that were NOT RUN, or only on legs that were run and could not complete? Round 2 fired it on 2 of 4 and I have fired it on 1 of 4 for consistency, but the item's own words are 'any run that cannot complete (O17)', and 'not run' and 'cannot complete' are different claims. The answer changes RI-JRN01 from 2 to somewhere in the 5-7 band and therefore changes this verdict's headline.

self_audit.aggregation_note: Ran the piece's own acceptance tools end to end (opening-play, census-newgame) rather than only my own arms, and verified the builder's pre-existing-failure claim at the BASE COMMIT in a worktree rather than accepting it.
self_audit.instrument_falsification: Three separate teardowns, each watched: (1) refusal = fault restored on a copy — 2/2 arms leak an engine string onto a drawn row; (2) real.textFocus forced true in the world — 13 control keys and 4 movement keys go dead; (3) bodyRace() pinned to a literal — 4 consumption arms collapse to 1. A fourth self-inflicted failure — my input probe reporting four dead movement keys because it read moveX/moveY AFTER the step consumed them — was caught by me, diagnosed, and is recorded in method_deviations rather than published as a finding.

notes: The honest shape of this round is that the builder was asked to close three blocking defects and closed all three, and that I could not break the two repairs it should have been hardest to trust: five throws from five places in the census path put nothing on a drawn row, and the text branch that now sits above the movement map changes nothing in the world when you remove it. The finding that matters is one layer under the fix that was made: the scribe now observes the body, which is right, but a body she cannot read is turned into `null` without a word and refused eleven nodes later at the desk — and at the base commit of this very round, the literal in that field was exactly such a body. The round fixed the value and left the mechanism. Everything else in this verdict is either an instrument that tests a narrower thing than it is being read as testing (P9's imperative regex, m4_clause1's driver pacing, walkTo's world_was_running, P10's name) or a modality leg nobody has run. None of it stops a person playing the game, and a person can now play the game: I did it twice, through the one command, in about three minutes, and the picture of a thirty-seven-letter name sitting in the field with the barge hold rendered behind it is the answer to the question the owner actually asked.
